verdict: A quiet day: one small but real ComfyUI tool update for MiniMax-H3, two solid studio virtual-production/VFX breakdowns, and otherwise mostly research-paper noise and entertainment trade news with nothing to act on.

stories.headline: MiniMax-H3 Turbo gets a dedicated ComfyUI LoRA node
stories.body: A Hugging Face repo packages a MiniMax-H3-Turbo LoRA as a ComfyUI-ready node under Apache-2.0 licence. It builds on the existing MiniMax-H3 text-to-video pipeline the reader already tracks, adding a turbo/speed variant that studios could drop into existing ComfyUI workflows. Low download count so far and no independent benchmarks; treat as early and unverified until someone reports real VRAM numbers and output quality.
stories.why: Extends an already-adopted open video model with a deployable speed option for studio ComfyUI pipelines.

stories.headline: Framestore details year-long virtual production build for Project Hail Mary
stories.body: Framestore describes how a six-week visualisation assignment on Project Hail Mary grew into a year-long virtual production collaboration at Shepperton, including immersive virtual environments and camera technology integrated directly with the live shoot. The piece is vendor-sourced but goes into the actual production workflow rather than marketing language, covering how the team worked alongside directors Lord and Miller.
stories.why: Concrete account of how a major facility scopes and scales a VP engagement end to end.

stories.headline: Proof's London studio details Coyote vs. Acme postvis workflow
stories.body: Proof's London team spent seven weeks producing 92 postvis ('Sketch-Vis') shots across five sequences for the Looney Tunes live-action/hybrid feature Coyote vs. Acme. The studio also opened a New York office, with Ari Aster's next film as its first project. Technical detail is thin but the shot-count and timeline figures are specific and primary-sourced.
stories.why: Gives a rare data point on postvis shot throughput and turnaround for hybrid live-action/animation work.
